items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3039

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the Erie county tax act, in relation to providing that
the amount required to redeem real property affected by any tax sale
certificate in foreclosure, or to be recovered by the plaintiff in
foreclosure, shall include the aggregate amount of all tax sale
certificates affecting such real property and shall also include
amounts for attorneys' fees, abstracts of title, court costs,
allowances and other disbursements


 PURPOSE :
To provide that the amount required to redeem real property affected
by any tax sale certificate in foreclosure, or to be recovered by the
plaintiff in foreclosure, shall include the aggregate amount of all
tax sale certificates affecting such real property and shall also
include amounts for reasonable and necessary attorneys' fees,
abstracts of title, court costs, allowances and other disbursements.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This bill would amend Sections 8-1.0, 8-2.0, 98.0, 11-4.0 and 11-12.0
of the Erie County Tax Act so as to provide that the amount required
to redeem real property affected by any Erie County tax sale
certificate in foreclosure, or to be recovered by the plaintiff in
such foreclosure, shall include the aggregate amount of all tax sale
certificates affecting such real property, together with amounts for
reasonable and necessary attorney's fees, abstracts of title, court
costs, allowances and other disbursements.

 JUSTIFICATION :
By requiring that the amount required to be paid to redeem such
property, and the amount to be recovered in foreclosure by the owner
of any Erie County tax sale certificate, shall include the full amount
of all such tax sale certificates so-owned, together with accrued
interest, penalties and the costs and expenses of foreclosure such as
reasonable and necessary attorneys' fees, court costs and abstracts of
title, the value and enforceability of Erie County tax sale
certificates offered for sale will be significantly enhanced.

Similarly, insofar as Erie County may find itself continuing to own
tax sale certificates, and thus needing to directly enforce the
collection of tax delinquencies under the in rem tax foreclosure
provisions of the Erie County Tax Act, the legislation also
specifically provides for the payment or recovery of a per parcel "in
rem fee" of not more than five hundred dollars so as to cover the
presumptive costs to Erie County for reasonable and necessary
attorneys' fees, abstracts of title and other disbursements for such
in rem tax foreclosures.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2008: S.6677-B/A.8345-C, passed the Senate.  However, the Erie County
Tax Act, originally enacted as Chapter 812 of the Laws of 1942, was
last amended by Chapter 8 of the laws of 2006 so as to allow for the
receipt by local tax collectors of partial payments toward current
fiscal year real property taxes.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Enhancement of the inherent value of Erie County tax sale
certificates, whether offered for sale or retained by Erie County, by
including foreclosure expenses such as reasonable and necessary
attorneys' fees, abstract of title, court costs, allowances and other
disbursements in the amount to be paid to redeem affected properties,
and the amount to be recovered in foreclosure, thereby removing the
financial burden of such reasonable and necessary expenses from the
owners of Erie County tax sale certificates.
 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided that sections two,
three, four and five of this act shall not affect or apply to any Erie
county tax sale certificates for any fiscal year prior to 2009.
